steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Material categories: woods (hardwood, softwood, manufactured), metals (ferrous, non-ferrous), polymers (thermoplastic, thermoset), ceramics.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Manufacturing processes: subtractive (CNC, laser cutting), additive (3D printing), forming (vacuum forming, injection moulding).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Material properties determine suitability: strength, weight, flexibility, durability, cost, sustainability and aesthetic qualities.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Joining methods: permanent (welding, adhesive, rivets) and temporary (screws, bolts, nuts) — choose based on function and disassembly needs.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring materials and manufacturing. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with materials and manufacturing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with materials and manufacturing. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to materials and manufacturing, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outc | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
